'''Wreaken Mining Rig Field Tests''' was a linked three-part field-test programme in ''Elite Dangerous'', run by Wreaken Corporation and [[Vodel]] at '''Metz Enterprise''' in the '''Ega''' system. It began with separate asteroid-mining and surface-mining Community Goals, then concluded with a sourced-materials goal for output-quality comparison tests.<ref name="frontier-cg">[https://www.elitedangerous.com/community/goals Community goals], Frontier Developments. Campaign details accessed 2026-09-14; conclusion checked 2026-09-17.</ref><ref name="galnet-tests">[https://www.elitedangerous.com/news/galnet/wreaken-calls-for-surface-mining-support-tests Wreaken Calls for Surface Mining Support Tests], GalNet, Frontier Developments, 3 September 3312. Accessed 2026-09-05.</ref><ref name="galnet-results">[https://www.elitedangerous.com/news/galnet/srv-and-surface-mining-trials-deemed-resounding-success SRV and Surface Mining Trials Deemed Resounding Success], GalNet, Frontier Developments, 17 September 3312. Accessed 2026-09-20.</ref>

All three goals used the same station but tracked different contribution rules. The first two phases required asteroid-mined or surface-mined cargo; the final phase asked commanders to obtain specified commodities from nearby external markets and sell them at Metz. During the opening weekend, several metals also sold at unusually high event-enhanced prices; that separate trading activity is covered as historical market context below.

== Event background ==

Wreaken has been developing deployable mining equipment for planetary work: rigs that can be set up on the surface, extract resources, and feed into a refinery module. Vodel's Rhino is the vehicle built to carry that idea into the field. GalNet described the Rhino as a large, heavily armoured SRV from Vodel, a Core Dynamics subsidiary, with deployable mining rigs and a refinery module fitted as standard for planetside mining.<ref name="galnet-rhino">[https://www.elitedangerous.com/news/galnet/vodel-reveals-new-srv-rhino Vodel Reveals New SRV Rhino], GalNet, Frontier Developments, 3 September 3312. Accessed 2026-09-05.</ref>

The Ega trials are where that technology stops being a showroom feature and starts being tested by pilots at scale. Dr. Ben Curtis, Wreaken's Chief Geologist, described the work as a way to test the rig's mining-laser technology and learn which materials it can extract from different planetary body types.<ref name="galnet-tests" /> Earlier GalNet coverage tied the project to Wreaken research into surface extraction, deployable drills, refinery modules, and surface scanning for planetary mining sites.<ref name="galnet-research">[https://www.elitedangerous.com/news/galnet/research-sheds-new-light-on-industrial-mining Research Sheds New Light on Industrial Mining], GalNet, Frontier Developments, 24 August 3312. Accessed 2026-09-05.</ref>

The original asteroid-mining goal gave Wreaken a baseline for comparison with the new surface-mining loop. The follow-up sourced-materials goal extended the testing programme by asking commanders to deliver specified commodities from external markets for output-quality comparison. For the details of deploying the Rhino, locating deposits, extracting resources, and recovering the rig, see [[Surface Mining with the Rhino]].

== Community Goals associated with the field tests ==

Metz Enterprise hosted three related Community Goals as part of the field-test programme. The asteroid-mining and surface-mining goals finished on 10 September 2026, followed by the sourced-materials comparison goal on 17 September 2026. Pilots had to register for each goal separately; joining one did not automatically join another. The targets, accepted cargo, contribution method and price multiplier differed between phases.<ref name="frontier-cg" /><ref name="inara-cg" />

=== Wreaken Calls for Sourced Materials for Output Quality Comparison Tests ===

'''Wreaken Calls for Sourced Materials for Output Quality Comparison Tests''' was the final phase of the field-test programme. Wreaken Corporation and Vodel asked commanders to source requested commodities from nearby external markets and sell them at Metz Enterprise for output-quality comparison testing.<ref name="frontier-cg" />

While the goal was active, participating commanders registered at Metz Enterprise before selling any of the following commodities:

{| class="wikitable"
! Sourced-materials CG commodities
|-
| Palladium, Gold, Silver, Bertrandite, Indite, Gallite, Coltan, Uraninite, Lepidolite, Cobalt, Rutile, Water
|}

Frontier's Community Goal data listed a target of '''350,000,000 tonnes''' and a temporary '''3x price multiplier''' for requested commodities sold as part of the initiative.<ref name="frontier-cg" /> This was a sourcing-and-delivery phase: commanders did not need to mine the commodities themselves, but had to register before a sale counted. The phase ended on '''17 September 2026''', and its temporary 3x multiplier ended with the campaign.

Inara's final community-tracked figures record '''Tier 3/5''', '''140,456,277 tonnes delivered''' and '''11,031 contributors'''. These are community-tracked results, not an official Frontier results statement.<ref name="inara-cg" />

=== Wreaken Calls for Mining Support to Test New Rig ===

'''Wreaken Calls for Mining Support to Test New Rig''' was the conventional mining side of the trial. Wreaken asked pilots to laser-mine asteroids so the company could compare normal asteroid yields with the new surface-mining system.<ref name="frontier-cg" />

'''This goal finished on 10 September 2026.''' To contribute while it was active, commanders registered at Metz Enterprise, mined qualifying asteroid commodities with laser mining, returned to Metz, and sold the cargo through the commodity market. Frontier's event data listed a target of '''35,000,000 tonnes''' and a '''6x price multiplier''' for commodities sold as part of the initiative.<ref name="frontier-cg" />

The asteroid goal accepted:

{| class="wikitable"
! Asteroid-mining CG commodities
|-
| Platinum, Palladium, Gold, Silver, Bertrandite, Indite, Gallite, Coltan, Uraninite, Lepidolite, Cobalt, Rutile, Water, Painite, Osmium, Praseodymium, Bromellite, Samarium
|}

The goal is now historical. Inara recorded '''5,929,716 of 35,000,000''' contributions and '''Tier 1/9''' when it finished. Those figures and its final contribution brackets should be treated as the result of the completed goal, not current progress.<ref name="inara-cg" />

=== Wreaken Calls for Surface Mining Support to Test New Rig ===

'''Wreaken Calls for Surface Mining Support to Test New Rig''' was the Rhino side of the event. This goal was built around Wreaken's deployable surface-mining rig rather than ordinary asteroid mining. After registering at Metz Enterprise, participating pilots sold raw or refined surface-mined materials to the station market.<ref name="frontier-cg" />

'''This goal finished on 10 September 2026.''' Frontier's event data listed a target of '''10,000,000 tonnes''' and an '''8x price multiplier''' for materials sold as part of this surface-mining initiative.<ref name="frontier-cg" />

The surface-mining goal accepted:

{| class="wikitable"
! Surface-mining CG commodities
|-
| Iridium, Helium, Helium-3, Bastnasite, Deuterium, Thortveitite, Quartz Pyroxenite, Olivine, Periclase Dunite, Sapphire, Diamond, Ruby, Magnesite
|}

These materials were tied to the Rhino and deployable-rig loop, not laser mining in asteroid rings. Inara recorded '''3,739,597 of 10,000,000''' contributions and '''Tier 5/9''' when the goal finished. Commanders unfamiliar with the system can find the deployment, extraction, refining, and recovery process in [[Surface Mining with the Rhino]].<ref name="inara-cg" />

== How participation worked ==

Participants travelled to '''Ega''' and docked at '''Metz Enterprise'''. Inara listed Metz as a Coriolis starport with large pads, a commodity market, shipyard, outfitting, repair, refuel, rearm and other major station services, approximately 5,392 Ls from the arrival point.<ref name="inara-metz" />

Each phase required commanders to register through the Community Goal panel before making qualifying sales. For the final phase, they sourced the requested commodities from an external market, returned to Metz Enterprise and sold them through the commodity market. All three goals are now closed to contributions.

=== Community Goal contribution vs ordinary trading ===

Not every sale at Metz counted as Community Goal progress.

A valid contribution required prior registration, and the cargo had to satisfy the relevant goal's rules. The asteroid phase required laser asteroid-mined commodities, the surface phase required materials from the Rhino/deployable-rig loop, and the sourced-materials phase required commodities obtained from nearby external markets.<ref name="frontier-cg" />

Ordinary trade and CG contribution were not always the same thing. During the opening weekend, purchased Gold, Palladium, Silver, Cobalt, Praseodymium and other normally tradable metals could be bought elsewhere and resold at Metz at event-enhanced prices. That did not advance the asteroid-mining goal because it was not mined cargo. The final phase differed because externally sourced commodities were its stated contribution method, provided the commander registered first.

== Rewards ==

All three completed goals listed the same minimum participation items. Frontier's Community Goal data stated that pilots who registered at least one contribution were eligible for:<ref name="frontier-cg" />

== Event duration and status ==

GalNet announced the field tests on 3 September 3312 and directed independent pilots to register at Metz Enterprise in Ega.<ref name="galnet-tests" /> The asteroid-mining and surface-mining goals ended on 10 September 2026. The separate sourced-materials phase ended on 17 September 2026, concluding the full three-part campaign.<ref name="frontier-cg" /><ref name="inara-cg" />

== Official follow-up ==

Frontier described the Rhino and surface-mining trials as a resounding success. Its closing statement said pilot telemetry showed that the Rhino performed across rough planetary terrain and that the quantity of minerals received from the surface-mining rig was unprecedented.<ref name="galnet-results" /> Frontier did not publish a detailed comparison between surface mining, asteroid mining and market-sourced deliveries, nor did it announce a mining-rig rebalance or permanent commodity-price or mining-economy changes.

== Market effects ==

The field tests had a much bigger effect on Ega than the mining objectives alone. The final sourced-materials phase applied a temporary '''3x price multiplier''' to requested commodities sold as part of the initiative. That multiplier ended with the campaign on 17 September 2026.<ref name="frontier-cg" /><ref name="inara-cg" />

The opening-weekend effect came from the original Community Goal pricing. Frontier's event data gave the asteroid-mining goal a 6x multiplier and the surface-mining goal an 8x multiplier for commodities sold as part of those initiatives.<ref name="frontier-cg" /> Those goals finished on 10 September; the separate 3x sourced-materials multiplier then ended with the final phase on 17 September.

=== Historical event-enhanced metals ===

The opening-weekend market surge affected multiple commodities in the game's metal category. The metals associated with the Wreaken field tests and showing event-enhanced pricing were Cobalt, Gold, Iridium, Osmium, Palladium, Platinum, Praseodymium, Samarium and Silver. Iridium belonged to the Rhino/surface-mining side; the other listed metals were associated with the asteroid-mining Community Goal where applicable. They were not all equally useful for ordinary station-to-Metz arbitrage, since some were primarily or exclusively obtained through mining while others could be sourced through ordinary commodity markets.

The following September 7 figures were observed directly in-game at Metz Enterprise by CMDR Sythan.<ref name="sythan-metals">Direct in-game observation by CMDR Sythan while docked at Metz Enterprise in Ega on 7 September 2026.</ref> They document the broader event-enhanced market and should not be read as a promise that every metal offered the same arbitrage opportunity:

|-

|-

|-
| Iridium || 1,038,104 Cr/t || approximately 908,340 Cr/t || Rhino/surface mining
|-

|-

|}

<ref name="sythan-metals">Direct in-game observation by CMDR Sythan while docked at Metz Enterprise in Ega on 7 September 2026.</ref>

Palladium was one of the clearest numerical examples of the wider opening-weekend metals surge. On 5 September 2026, Inara showed Metz Enterprise buying Palladium for '''302,136 Cr/t''' with '''999,999 t''' of displayed demand.<ref name="inara-palladium">[https://inara.cz/elite/commodity/45/ Palladium - commodity], Inara. Accessed 2026-09-05.</ref> That price is an event-driven snapshot, not Palladium's normal value. A direct in-game observation by CMDR Sythan while docked at Metz Enterprise on 7 September 2026 recorded Palladium at '''75,534 Cr/t''', with '''999,999 t''' of displayed demand and a displayed Galactic Average of approximately '''25,180 Cr/t'''. Compared with the 5 September price, that was a reduction of '''226,602 Cr/t''' or '''75%'''. This records the change for Palladium specifically; it does not establish that every event-enhanced commodity price has ended.

At the same time, Inara's Palladium page listed a trade route from Black Moon Terminus buying at '''47,872 Cr/t''' and selling at Metz Enterprise for '''302,136 Cr/t'''. That left more than 254,000 credits of gross margin on every tonne hauled to Ega.<ref name="inara-palladium" />

{| class="wikitable"
! Item !! Example value
|-
| Source buy price || 47,872 Cr/t
|-
| Metz sell price || 302,136 Cr/t
|-
| Gross spread || 254,264 Cr/t
|-
| 720 t cargo example || 183,070,080 Cr gross spread before expenses and delays
|-
| 784 t cargo example || 199,342,976 Cr gross spread before expenses and delays
|}

Those figures explain why Ega drew so much attention during the opening-weekend metals trading rush, but they are historical snapshots. Prices, supply, and route quality can move quickly, and the real return depends on cargo capacity, travel time, supercruise distance, traffic, interdictions, market data age, and whether the cargo is being moved directly or through carrier logistics.

=== Historical September 7 multiplier change ===

On 7 September, Frontier reduced the extreme opening-weekend multipliers specifically affecting Gold, Palladium and Silver: Gold fell from 6x to 1.5x, Palladium from 6x to 1.5x, and Silver from 6x to 2x. This brought the extraordinary opening-weekend ordinary-market arbitrage rush to an end. The September 7 observations above document the historical market effect; they are not prices from the later sourced-materials phase.

Palladium provides the clearest comparison. The 5 September example used 302,136 Cr/t at Metz and a source price of 47,872 Cr/t, producing the historical 254,264 Cr/t gross spread shown above. Using the separately observed source price around 48,678 Cr/t, the opening-weekend comparison was approximately 253,000 Cr/t, while the 7 September Palladium price produced approximately 26,856 Cr/t before expenses. The historical margins describe 5 September conditions and should not be treated as currently available returns.

=== Historical Fleet Carrier trading ===

During the opening-weekend metals trading rush, [[Fleet Carrier|Fleet Carriers]] amplified the same trade dramatically. Instead of moving one shipload from the source to Ega, a carrier owner could stage tens of thousands of tonnes near a cheap Palladium market, jump the entire stockpile to Ega, and unload it into Metz Enterprise while the extreme event price remained favourable.

Using the observed 5 September 2026 Palladium prices above, a carrier operation moving 20,000 tonnes would have looked like this:

{| class="wikitable"
! Calculation !! Value
|-
| Destination price || 302,136 Cr/t
|-
| Source price || 47,872 Cr/t
|-
| Gross spread per tonne || 254,264 Cr/t
|-
| Cargo moved || 20,000 t
|-
| Gross market spread || 5,085,280,000 Cr
|}

That was gross market spread, not guaranteed profit. Loading time, available carrier capacity, Tritium, carrier services, price movement, and any margin paid to other haulers still came out of the operation.

=== Historical PTN and player-operated logistics ===

Player groups reacted to the opening-weekend spread as well. The Pilots Trade Network, for example, was visible in Inara market data around Ega through carriers and trade listings tied to Palladium movement.<ref name="inara-palladium" /> The practical idea was simple: a carrier operator acquired cargo in bulk, moved it close to the high-price market, and paid haulers to shuttle the final loads between the carrier and Metz Enterprise.

The large historical spread left room for both sides to earn credits when the numbers lined up. That activity was player logistics, not an official part of the Community Goal, and EDFM is not affiliated with PTN. Unloading bought cargo from a carrier was ordinary trade unless the cargo also satisfied the actual CG contribution rules.

=== Historical solo trading ===

A Fleet Carrier or PTN job was not required to participate in the opening-weekend metals surge. If Palladium, Gold, Silver or another normally tradable metal was available cheaply enough elsewhere, a pilot could buy it, fly directly to Metz Enterprise, and sell into the elevated market.

Those routes depended entirely on the temporary live numbers. The historical figures here should not be used as a current route guide: bought cargo could produce ordinary trade profit during the surge, but it did not count as mined Community Goal contribution.

== Why this event matters ==

Even without the extraordinary trade profits, the Wreaken Mining Rig Field Tests are an important moment for the Rhino. They put the deployable mining-rig system into large-scale public use and place the new surface-mining loop directly beside the asteroid mining players have used for years.

For several days during the opening weekend, Ega was also the centre of an extraordinary metals trading and Fleet Carrier logistics boom. The follow-up sourced-materials phase extended the output-comparison work through commodity sourcing rather than a new mining objective. Frontier later described the field trials as a resounding success and said the Rhino had performed across the roughest planetary terrain.<ref name="galnet-results" /> The response around Metz Enterprise — mined deliveries, sourced-materials deliveries, direct arbitrage, Fleet Carrier hauling and player-run logistics — is part of the event's history alongside the final contribution totals.
